tasks.short: Inspect baked goods, find what expires today, remove damaged or expired goods and record waste.

steps.what: Baker inspects baked goods for colour, shape and bake
Baker reads dates on shelves and in stock to identify expired goods
Baker removes damaged or expired goods from sale
Baker writes removed goods on the waste sheet

tasks.design: Batch labels printed at packing carry a use-by date, and the shop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists which batches expire today, so the baker goes straight to them instead of reading every date. Removed goods are booked as waste with one scan at the till. Judging quality and removing goods stay with the baker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were read item by item and waste written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Label printers put batch and use-by date on goods; shop systems list what expires.
tasks.still_hard: Damage and poor bakes are seen, not scanned.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a tray of rolls is underbaked before a customer does.

evidence.claim: Label printers put batch and use-by date on goods, and shop systems list what expires.
Stock and sales records are basic records kept seven years.

assumptions: Boundary: from inspecting goods to the waste record; donating surplus is outside.
Input contract: batch labels printed at packing; shelf lives set by the head baker; fallback is reading dates.
Inspecting and removing do not change.
Waste scans are about products, not used to rate staff.
research_questions: Does waste fall once expiry is listed?

incremental.description: Baker labels each batch at packing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is looking at goods.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check machines for safe working, clean them, tick the cleaning schedule, log fridge temperatures and report faults.

steps.what: Baker checks ovens, mixers and slicers to ensure they meet health and safety regulations
Baker performs cleaning of equipment per the cleaning schedule
Baker ticks the paper cleaning schedule
Baker reads and writes down fridge and freezer temperatures
Baker reports faults to the maintenance company

tasks.design: Each machine has a QR code; scanning it on the bakery tablet ({OTHER}) shows its cleaning steps and records the clean with time and name. Wireless sensors log fridge and freezer temperatures to the same food safety app. Checking, cleaning and reporting faults stay with the baker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cleaning and temperatures were recorded on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Food safety apps take QR scans and wireless sensor readings.
tasks.still_hard: A tick is not a clean; inspections still look at the machine.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a mixer bearing is about to fail.

reach.learn: Whether QR scans keep records complete.

evidence.claim: Food safety apps take QR scans per machine and wireless temperature sensor readings.
Food businesses must keep records of their cleaning and temperature checks.

assumptions: Boundary: from checking equipment to faults reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: cleaning steps per machine set by the head baker; fallback is paper lists.
Checking, cleaning and reporting do not change.
Names on cleaning records are not used to rate staff.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is cleaning by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Total the day's orders, scale recipes, adjust for flour and weather, weigh ingredients and note batch quantities.

steps.what: Baker totals the day's orders and shop needs per product
Baker adapts the quantity of ingredients to match the amount of items by hand calculation
Baker adjusts for flour moisture, weather and dough behaviour
Baker writes batch quantities on the production sheet

tasks.design: The bakery's production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) totals customer orders and shop needs per product, and scales each recipe by baker's percentages to the day's quantities, printing a weigh list per batch. The baker adjusts water and timing for the flour and weather and weighs; the production record is kept from the weigh list. No model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were totalled and recipes scaled by hand each morning.
tasks.enabler_now: Bakery production systems keep formulas and scale them to order quantities.
tasks.still_hard: Dough behaves differently every day; scaling is only the start.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that today's dough needs less water.

reach.learn: Whether weigh lists cut scaling errors.

evidence.claim: Aptean Bakery ERP keeps formulas, flags allergens and shows cost per product.
In 2021 about half of 1,910 inspected artisan producers did not give correct allergen information; scaled recipes must keep the allergen table.

assumptions: Boundary: from orders to the production record; baking is outside.
Input contract: customer orders from the shop and web orders; formulas kept by the head baker; fallback is hand calculation.
Adjusting and weighing do not change.
Shop staff time is outside the baker's savings.
research_questions: Do scaling errors and over-production fall?

incremental.description: Head baker keeps formulas current in the system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Bakeries that already scale in a spreadsheet save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check deliveries, compare them with the order and specs, test raw materials, record lot numbers and return rejected goods.

steps.what: Baker checks deliveries for damage, temperature and dates
Baker compares delivered goods with the order and specifications
Baker checks the quality of raw materials by smell, look and test bake
Baker writes lot numbers on the goods-in sheet
Baker phones the supplier to return rejected goods

tasks.design: Deliveries are scanned against the order in the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which shows differences and the spec limits per raw material, and scanning lot barcodes records supplier, lot and date for traceability. Checking deliveries, testing quality and returns stay with the baker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were compared on paper and lot numbers copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Goods-in apps scan delivery labels and lot barcodes.
tasks.still_hard: Flour quality shows in the dough, not on the label.
tasks.human_edge: Smelling that a batch of butter has turned.

reach.learn: Whether lot scans make recalls faster.

evidence.claim: Goods-in apps scan delivery labels and lot barcodes into traceability records.
Food businesses must record description, quantity, supplier, lot and dispatch date, one step back and one step forward.

assumptions: Boundary: from delivery to return arranged; supplier choice is outside.
Input contract: orders placed in the production system by the head baker; spec limits set by the head baker; lot barcodes on suppliers' labels; fallback is paper.
Checking, testing and returns do not change.
Suppliers without lot barcodes are entered by hand.
research_questions: Can a recall be traced within an hour?

incremental.description: Baker types lots for suppliers without barcodes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is checking by senses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The baker keeps judging dough, goods and raw materials; scaling, totals and paper records go.
skills_to_grow: Keeping formulas current in the system
role.ambitious_version: A baker who starts the morning with weigh lists ready and spends the time on the dough.
